summary: Atlas (Kickstarter, ZYVORALABS LIMITED, Hong Kong; campaign 16 Sep–16 Oct 2026, 912 backers / ~EUR 125k on 21 Sep, est. delivery Mar 2027) is, per its own spec image, an ESP32-C5 (16 MB flash, 8 MB PSRAM) + 8 GB storage + 7.5" 800x480 e-paper slab, 191x127x10 mm, ~180 g, portrait UI, side power button, CT-800 engine (~2200 Elo), Lichess only (Chess.com 'being evaluated'), no subscription, OTA updates; battery is stated inconsistently (4000 mAh in spec image, 2000 mAh in FAQ/website). I read the full FAQ, reward tiers, updates, creator comments and the image-only campaign story via browser screenshots and built a feature checklist. Our roadmap covers the core (engine, Lichess seek/live game, Lichess puzzles, PGN replay, OTA) but is missing: local two-player mode, challenge-a-friend / receive-invites / play-vs-Lichess-AI, OFFLINE puzzles, a lessons library (openings/defence/endgames/classics) with 'take over any position vs engine', undo + move-list navigation, analysis/review, PGN upload from phone, and a wake/power button UX. The planned pin map puts touch INT on GPIO43, which is not an RTC GPIO on ESP32-S3 (RTC = GPIO0-21, verified in local soc_caps.h), so deep-sleep wake-on-touch is impossible as wired; cheap to fix now. Release channel: MakerWorld Exclusive (+25% points, 90-day lock-in) forces Standard Digital File or MakerWorld Exclusive License and forbids publishing the 3D files anywhere else, which conflicts with an 'open' STEP-on-GitHub release; non-exclusive CC licensing coexists fine with GPL-3.0 firmware on GitHub (separate works; a live MakerWorld 7.5" ESP32 e-paper model already links its GitHub repo). Web flasher: ESP Web Tools supports ESP32-S3 incl. serialType 'cdc'; pioarduino 55.03.38 already auto-generates firmware.factory.bin, BUT it stamps the header with the board JSON flash size and ESP Web Tools flashes with flashSize 'keep' -> with the current platformio.ini (board = seeed_xiao_esp32s3 = 8MB + default_16MB.csv) a web-flashed device will fail partition validation at boot even though 'pio run -t upload' works (it uses --flash-size detect). Prior art: ChuckJonas/crosscheck (MIT) is a working Lichess Board-API client on almost identical hardware (ESP32-S3, 8 MB PSRAM, 480x800 e-ink, GT911) and its dev notes contain measured lessons (562 ms full-frame fast refresh, periodic full refresh removed because it read as random flashes, Lichess rejects open seeks under ~8 min, idle connections dropped after ~10 s, heap 144 KB with two streams). Naming: do not ship under 'Atlas' or as a 'replica'; use an own name plus nominative 'inspired by / alternative to' wording and a non-affiliation disclaimer, as CrossPoint and FreeDeck do.

findings.claim: Atlas internals and physical specs are published by the creator: ESP32-C5 (Flash 16 MB, external RAM 8 MB), 8 GB storage, 7.5" 800x480 e-ink, '<300 ms optimized move updates', 191 x 127 x 10 mm, ~180 g, CT-800 engine, Wi-Fi, USB-C (C-to-C cable in box), side power button, white or black. Battery capacity is contradictory between creator sources (4000 mAh vs 2000 mAh). No frontlight, speaker or physical buttons other than power are mentioned anywhere.
findings.evidence: Campaign spec image 'Designed Around Chess' (read via screenshot): 'SPEED <300 ms optimized move updates / PROCESSOR ESP32-C5 Flash: 16 MB, External RAM: 8MB / ENGINE CT-800 Chess Engine / WEIGHT ~180 g / STORAGE 8 GB / BATTERY 4000 mAh / DIMENSIONS 191 x 127 x 10 mm / DISPLAY 7.5" E-Ink - 800 x 480'; splash screen in same image: 'ATLAS E-Ink Smart Chess ... Press the power button to wake'. Kickstarter FAQ 'How long does the battery last?': 'Atlas features a 2,000 mAh battery and can provide up to 7 days of typical usage on a single charge.' atlas-chess.com repeats 2000 mAh. Rewards list '1x C-to-C charging cable', 'Color: White/Black', '1-Year Warranty'. Section title 'Chess, Without the Glow' (no backlight marketing). INFERENCE (not stated by creator): same panel class as our GDEY075T7 (same size/resolution); panel and touch part numbers are not disclosed.
findings.recommended_action: Use 191x127x10 mm / ~180 g as the case benchmark (our recap expects 15-16 mm). Our XIAO ESP32-S3 Plus (dual core, 16 MB/8 MB) is at least equal to the C5 on compute; the only hardware Atlas has that we lack is mass storage (8 GB) and a power/wake button. Plan offline content to fit the 3.4 MB LittleFS partition of default_16MB.csv or a custom table with a larger FS.

findings.claim: Complete Atlas feature/UI checklist (from FAQ text + UI screenshots). HOME: greeting with account name, 'Random Play (Lichess)', 'Lichess', 'Atlas Essentials', 'Settings'. LICHESS menu: Random Play, Challenge a Friend, With Bot, Puzzles/Daily Puzzles, Settings, Receive Invites. ESSENTIALS menu: Play with Engine, Over-the-board (local 2-player), Lessons = Openings (Italian, Ruy Lopez, Scotch, Vienna, Four Knights, London, Catalan, Colle, paged 1/2), Defence, Endgames ('Closings'), Classics. IN-GAME screen (portrait): top bar 'Back' + title + Wi-Fi and battery icons, opponent label and clock (e.g. 'BOT 9:48'), 480 px board, SAN move strip with left/right arrows, 'Undo' button. Interaction: tap-tap; long-press a piece shows legal moves ('Move Assist', optional). Engine: CT-800 'up to ~2200 Elo', multiple levels, 'dynamically adjust the engine's playing strength'. Puzzles both online (Lichess) and offline. Replay: PGN uploaded from phone/computer, classic games, own games; 'Play From Any Position: pause, take over and continue vs CT-800'. 'Analysis'. Full move validation. OTA firmware updates (creator comment, cadence 'once every 3-4 months'). Platforms: Lichess only; Chess.com 'currently being evaluated', would come as firmware update. No subscription. Accessories: standard case, case with stand, zip sleeve.
findings.evidence: FAQ quotes: 'Built-in CT-800 chess engine rated up to ~2200 Elo'; 'Atlas Essentials - structured chess learning with Openings, Defence, Closings, and Classics'; 'Play random opponents / Challenge friends or specific players / Play against online bots / Solve chess puzzles / Access your Lichess account directly from Atlas'; 'Play two-player local games / Practice offline chess puzzles'; 'To see legal moves, simply press and hold a piece'; 'uploading a PGN file from your account, you may use a phone or computer to upload the file to Atlas'; 'Chess.com integration is currently being evaluated. We have provided an Atlas device to the Chess.com team'; 'Is there a subscription fee? No'. Creator comment: 'we can deliver improvements, bug fixes, and supported feature updates through OTA (over-the-air) firmware updates'. Menu items and in-game layout read from campaign images 600541ea..., 96b2fc7d..., 55671efe..., 0c2c106f..., 7145e8bc..., 28426ec8..., 8570cb43..., f210229f... Time controls supported, Lichess login method, sound and frontlight are NOT documented anywhere I could read.
findings.recommended_action: Adopt this list as the parity checklist in the repo (docs/parity.md) and tick items per phase. Do not copy their menu wording ('Atlas Essentials', 'Random Play') or screen layout pixel-for-pixel; keep function, change naming and visual design.

findings.claim: Atlas features absent from our 5-step roadmap: (1) local two-player 'over-the-board' mode; (2) Lichess challenge flows: challenge a friend by name, receive/accept invites, play Lichess AI/bots (roadmap only says 'seek, live game'); (3) OFFLINE puzzles (roadmap has only online Lichess puzzles); (4) lessons library (openings/defence/endgames/classic games) and 'take over any position against the engine'; (5) undo/takeback and move-list navigation during a game; (6) analysis/review mode; (7) a path to get PGN onto the device (Atlas: upload from phone/computer; we have no SD slot, so this means an on-device HTTP upload page to LittleFS); (8) power/wake button UX and sleep splash; (9) account greeting / Lichess account linking UX; (10) protective case/stand accessories (natural fit for Fabrizio's 3D side). Items in our roadmap that Atlas does not advertise: buzzer feedback, battery gauge (Atlas shows a battery icon, so parity), captive-portal setup.
findings.evidence: Roadmap from /Users/fabriziodrago/Downloads/RECAP-scacchiera-eink.md lines 50-55: '2. CT-800 offline, regole, promozione, orologio, bitmap pezzi 3. Lichess Board API (captive portal, token, seek, partita live) 4. Puzzle Lichess, replay PGN, batteria, deep sleep, OTA'. Atlas FAQ: 'Play two-player local games', 'Practice offline chess puzzles', 'Challenge friends or specific players', 'Play against online bots'; Lichess menu screenshot shows 'Receive Invites'; image 28426ec8: 'Play From Any Position. Pause the game at any position. Take over. And continue playing that position against the CT-800 chess engine.' Offline puzzles are legally easy: database.lichess.org: 'Database exports are released under the Creative Commons CC0 license', 6,100,952 puzzles, CSV fields 'PuzzleId, FEN, Moves, Rating, ... Themes'. Lichess Board API (primary spec) supports 'Receive, create and accept (or decline) challenges' and 'For direct challenges, games vs AI, and bulk pairing, Blitz is also possible'. Chess.com parity is a non-issue: Atlas does not have it either (my understanding, not re-verified this session, is that Chess.com exposes only a read-only published-data API).
findings.recommended_action: Extend the roadmap: phase 2 += two-player local, undo, move-list navigation, 'play from position (FEN)'; phase 3 += challenge by username, accept/decline incoming challenges, challenge Lichess AI levels 1-8 (also the only way to get blitz); phase 4 += offline puzzle pack built from the CC0 Lichess puzzle CSV (a filtered 20-50k subset packs into ~2 MB), opening/classic-games pack from CC0 lichess-org/chess-openings and public-domain PGNs, on-device web page for PGN upload, sleep splash + wake button. Ask Fabrizio to rank these.

verification.corrected_claim: Confirmed Atlas features missing from the 5-step roadmap: two-player local play; Lichess 'challenge friends or specific players' and 'play against online bots'; OFFLINE puzzles; 'Atlas Essentials' lesson library (Openings, Defence, Closings/Endgames, Classics); 'Play From Any Position' vs CT-800; PGN upload from phone/computer + replay/review; power-button wake with sleep splash; 'Hello, <name>' account greeting; case-with-stand and sleeve accessories. Undo/takeback, move-list navigation, analysis mode and a 'Receive Invites' menu were NOT verified by me. Chess.com: not supported today, but Atlas states it has given a device to Chess.com and plans support via firmware update (a parity gap an open project cannot close, since Chess.com has no public play API). Blitz on Lichess Board API is possible via direct challenges AND vs AI, not only AI. Offline puzzle pack from the CC0 Lichess puzzle CSV (6,100,952 puzzles) is legally clean.
verification.reasoning: Re-read the Kickstarter FAQ DOM myself (WebFetch gets 403; used the browser pane). Verbatim: 'Play two-player local games', 'Practice offline chess puzzles', 'Explore Atlas Essentials, including Openings, Defence, Closings, and Classics', Lichess list 'Play random opponents / Challenge friends or specific players / Play against online bots / Solve chess puzzles / Access your Lichess account directly from Atlas', and 'uploading a PGN file from your account, you may use a phone or computer to upload the file to Atlas'. Campaign image 28426ec8 viewed: 'Upload A PGN File ... Study Your Own Games / Replay Important Games / Explore Classic Games' and 'Play From Any Position. Pause the game at any position. Take over. And continue playing that position against the CT-800 chess engine.' Image 8570cb43 shows home menu 'Hello, John / Random Play / Lichess / Atlas Essentials / Settings' (account greeting confirmed). Spec image 621457ed shows splash 'Press the power button to wake'. Rewards tab: 'Atlas Premium Protective Case with Stand' and 'Atlas Protective Sleeve'. Recap roadmap lines match the quote. database.lichess.org re-fetched: CC0, 6,100,952 puzzles, fields PuzzleId,FEN,Moves,Rating,RatingDeviation,Popularity,NbPlays,Themes,GameUrl,OpeningTags,DailyDate. Lichess API yaml re-fetched: 'Receive, create and accept (or decline) challenges' and 'Rapid, Classical and Correspondence only. For direct challenges, games vs AI, and bulk pairing, Blitz is also possible.' NOT personally verified: undo/takeback, move-list navigation, analysis/review mode and the 'Receive Invites' menu screenshot (I did not find those images; FAQ only says 'continue playing and reviewing it'). Two corrections: (a) Chess.com is NOT a permanent non-issue: FAQ says 'Chess.com integration is currently being evaluated. We have provided an Atlas device to the Chess.com team ... we plan to integrate Chess.com support ... delivered as a firmware update' - a partner integration an open project cannot get; (b) the recommended action says AI is 'the only way to get blitz' - the spec quote itself says direct challenges (friend) also allow blitz. Atlas lesson category is 'Closings', not 'endgames' (image says 'Openings - Endgames - Classics', FAQ says 'Openings, Defence, Closings, Classics').

findings.claim: Atlas wakes via a dedicated power button. Our BOM has only the driver board slide switch, and the planned pin map puts the GT911 INT on GPIO43 (D6) and RST on GPIO44 (D7); neither is an RTC GPIO on ESP32-S3, so ext0/ext1 deep-sleep wake from a touch is impossible with the wiring as planned (roadmap item 4 'deep sleep'). Only light sleep (any GPIO) or a power-cycle via the slide switch would resume the device.
findings.evidence: Local primary source: ~/.platformio/packages/framework-arduinoespressif32-libs/esp32s3/include/soc/esp32s3/include/soc/soc_caps.h:329 '#define SOC_RTCIO_PIN_COUNT 22' and rtc_io_channel.h ends at 'RTCIO_GPIO21_CHANNEL 21' -> RTC-capable = GPIO0..21. ~/.platformio/packages/framework-arduinoespressif32/variants/XIAO_ESP32S3_Plus/pins_arduino.h: 'D6 = 43', 'D7 = 44', 'D9 = 8', and Plus-only pads 'D16 = 10, D17 = 13, D18 = 12, D19 = 11' (RTC-capable but on the underside pads). src/config.h: '#define TP_INT 43 // D6', '#define BUZZER_PIN 8 // D9'. Atlas splash: 'Press the power button to wake'. INFERENCE: GPIO8/D9 is the only RTC-capable header pin not already taken by display/I2C in the current map; whether the Seeed driver board itself uses D9 or provides a button must be confirmed from its schematic (other thread). GT911 low-power behaviour (whether it still raises INT in its sleep/green modes) was not verified here.
findings.recommended_action: Decide the wake model before wiring. Option A (Atlas-like, most robust): add a tactile wake button to an RTC-capable pin and keep the slide switch as hard-off. Option B: swap signals so TP_INT lands on an RTC pin, e.g. TP_INT -> GPIO8 (D9), buzzer -> GPIO44 (D7, silent at boot because U0RXD is an input) and TP_RST -> GPIO43 (D6; ROM boot log toggles it, harmless because firmware re-runs the GT911 reset sequence). Note a passive buzzer on GPIO43 would chirp on every reset because the ROM prints the boot log on U0TXD. Validate against the driver-board schematic first.

verification.corrected_claim: As claimed: on ESP32-S3 only GPIO0-21 are RTC GPIOs (esp_sleep.h: 'ESP32-S3: 0-21'), so GT911 INT on GPIO43 (D6) / RST on GPIO44 (D7) cannot wake the chip from deep sleep; GPIO8 (D9, now the buzzer) is the only free RTC-capable header pin, and the Seeed driver board (uses only D0-D3, D8, D10; power slide switch only) does not conflict. Atlas uses a physical power button ('Press the power button to wake'). Extra options: the XIAO BOOT button is GPIO0 (RTC-capable) and can serve as ext0 wake button with no wiring; option B (TP_INT->GPIO8, TP_RST->GPIO43, buzzer->GPIO44) additionally removes the boot-log contention on the GT911 INT line. Touch-to-wake requires leaving the GT911 un-slept (standby current not verified).
verification.reasoning: Verified locally: soc_caps.h:329 '#define SOC_RTCIO_PIN_COUNT 22', rtc_io_channel.h ends at RTCIO_GPIO21_CHANNEL, and esp_sleep.h lines 271-272/315-316/364-365 state for ext0/ext1 'ESP32-S3: 0-21'. soc_caps.h has SOC_PM_SUPPORT_EXT0/EXT1_WAKEUP only (no SOC_GPIO_SUPPORT_DEEPSLEEP_WAKEUP on S3), so GPIO43/44 cannot wake from deep sleep. variants/XIAO_ESP32S3_Plus/pins_arduino.h: D6=43, D7=44, D9=8, D16=10, D17=13, D18=12, D19=11. config.h: TP_INT 43, TP_RST 44, BUZZER_PIN 8. Atlas spec image viewed: splash text 'Press the power button to wake' and a side button is visible. Seeed wiki re-fetched: driver board uses only D0,D1,D2,D3,D8,D10 and has 'Power switch: For battery power control' - no user button, D9 is free, so option B is not blocked by the driver board. Header pins that are RTC-capable = GPIO1-9; all but GPIO8 are taken by display/I2C, so the inference holds. Additions the researcher missed: (1) the XIAO's on-board BOOT button is GPIO0, which IS an RTC GPIO, so ext0 wake on GPIO0 via a printed plunger is a zero-wire wake button (inference from standard XIAO design; deep-sleep wake does not re-sample strapping pins, so it will not enter download mode - not tested); (2) with the current map, GT911 INT (an output in normal operation) sits on U0TXD/GPIO43, which the ROM and 2nd-stage bootloader drive with the boot log on every reset -> brief output-vs-output contention; moving TP_RST (an input on the GT911) to GPIO43 as in option B removes that too. Unverified: GT911 must stay in normal/green mode (mA-class current, not read in a datasheet by me) to raise INT on touch; in GT911 sleep mode it will not, so touch-to-wake costs standby current - a physical button is the low-power choice.

findings.claim: Atlas advertises '<300 ms optimized move updates' and states all campaign videos are real-time. With stock GxEPD2 on our exact panel class the library's nominal partial refresh is 450 ms (+140 ms power-on if the panel was powered off), and the closest open project measured 562 ms for a full-frame fast refresh. Matching Atlas will need windowed partial updates of only the 2-4 changed squares with the panel kept powered, and possibly a custom/faster LUT; this is the single most visible UX gap to plan for.
findings.evidence: Atlas spec image: 'SPEED <300 ms optimized move updates'; campaign image 5acf091c: 'All videos on this page are recorded in real time and shown at actual playback speed.' GxEPD2 src/gdey/GxEPD2_750_GDEY075T7.h: 'Controller: UC8179', 'hasFastPartialUpdate = true', 'power_on_time = 140', 'power_off_time = 42', 'full_refresh_time = 1200', 'partial_refresh_time = 450'. Crosscheck dev notes: 'Fast refresh takes 562 ms on the panel'; its spec expected 'partial refresh at 200-300 ms' and estimated 'device round-trip (touch -> Wi-Fi -> Lichess -> refresh) is ~0.5 s per move'.
findings.recommended_action: Keep the phase-1 on-screen ms counter (good idea) and make 'ms per move update' a tracked release metric with target <=300 ms. First experiments when hardware arrives: partial window limited to the two squares, no powerOff()/hibernate() between moves during a game, then evaluate UC8179 custom LUT registers if still >300 ms.

verification.corrected_claim: Atlas advertises '<300 ms optimized move updates' with real-time videos; Good Display's datasheet page for our exact panel (GDEY075T7) also states 'Partial refresh: 0.3s', so 300 ms is the vendor nominal, while GxEPD2's nominal for it is 450 ms (+140 ms power-on after each full refresh, since GxEPD2 powers off after full updates only). The phase-1 firmware as written does three separate partial refreshes per move (from-square, to-square, status) and will therefore take roughly 1.3 s per move, not 450 ms: merge them into a single partial refresh over the bounding box (refresh time on UC8179 does not shrink with window size), keep the panel powered during a game, then consider custom LUT / PLL frame-rate tuning to get from ~450 to <=300 ms. Crosscheck's 562 ms is a full-frame fast refresh on a different device (Xteink X4 Pro) and driver.
verification.reasoning: Viewed Atlas spec image: 'SPEED <300 ms optimized move updates'; image 5acf091c: 'REAL-TIME. REAL SPEED. All videos on this page are recorded in real time and shown at actual playback speed.' Re-fetched GxEPD2_750_GDEY075T7.h: Controller UC8179, hasFastPartialUpdate=true, power_on_time=140, power_off_time=42, full_refresh_time=1200, partial_refresh_time=450, useFastFullUpdate=true. The .cpp waits on BUSY ('_waitWhileBusy("_Update_Part", partial_refresh_time)'), so 450 ms is the author's nominal value, real time must be measured. GxEPD2_BW.h nextPage(): powerOff() is called after FULL updates only, not after partial -> the +140 ms applies to the first partial after each full refresh. Crosscheck dev notes re-fetched: 'A fast refresh takes 562 ms on the panel' (full frame, because 'the UC8179 driver of the X4 Pro does not implement [windowed refresh] and falls back to a full frame'; different driver and panel, Xteink X4 Pro); spec: expected partial refresh '200-300 ms', round trip '~0.5 s per move'. Additional evidence the researcher missed: Good Display's own GDEY075T7 product page lists 'Partial refresh: 0.3s' (full 3s, fast 1.5s), i.e. Atlas's '<300 ms' equals the vendor's nominal partial-refresh figure for our exact panel, so the target is realistic. IMPORTANT firmware finding: phase-1 main.cpp lines 71-75 issue THREE sequential partial refreshes per move (drawSquare from, drawSquare to, drawStatus), each a full waveform (~450 ms nominal) => ~0.9 s for the two squares + ~0.45 s status. On UC8179 the waveform duration is set by the LUT/frame rate, not by window area (inference from controller design), so the fix is ONE refresh over the bounding box of all changed squares (or the whole board), not per-square windows.

findings.claim: Atlas and Crosscheck both use portrait orientation: 480 px wide board = 60 px squares on top, clocks/move strip/buttons in the remaining 320 px below. Our phase-1 firmware is landscape (rotation 0) with a side column. Square size is identical either way (60 px = 12.2 mm on this panel), so this is purely a product/case decision, but it drives the case design (where the USB-C, switch, FPC tail and hand grip go) and must be fixed before Fabrizio models the shell.
findings.evidence: Atlas UI screenshots show portrait device with top bar, board, move strip and 'Undo' beneath. Crosscheck spec: 'Board rendered full-width (480 px -> 60 px squares), flipped for black, coordinates on edges, last move highlighted, check indicator.' Our firmware: src/main.cpp:32 'display.setRotation(0);' and gt911.cpp:43 comment 'il pannello touch e nativo 800x480 landscape; rotazioni per la scocca'. Recap: active area 163.2 x 97.9 mm -> 0.204 mm/px.
findings.recommended_action: Ask Fabrizio to choose portrait (handheld, e-reader feel, like Atlas) or landscape (desk stand, differentiates visually from Atlas). Make orientation a compile-time or settings option in the UI layer so the case can ship in both variants later.

findings.claim: Campaign facts: creator account 'Atlas-E-Ink Chess' (first project, 6 backed), Central, Hong Kong; legal entity on atlas-chess.com is ZYVORALABS LIMITED, Unit 2A 17/F Glenealy Tower, Hong Kong. Live 16 Sep - 16 Oct 2026 (all-or-nothing, goal EUR 8,713; EUR 125,040 from 912 backers on 21 Sep). Tiers: Super Early Bird HK$1,169 (~EUR 130 / ~US$149), Early Bird HK$1,326 (~EUR 148 / ~US$169), Duo HK$2,188 (~EUR 244); site lists Kickstarter price US$199 and regular US$249; pre-launch 'Founding Backer' price was US$129 (1,000 units). Shipping and EU VAT/duties are extra. Estimated delivery March 2027. Creator discloses AI-edited marketing imagery. Our parts cost (~EUR 89 + ~EUR 30 shipping) is roughly on par with an EU-landed Atlas, so the open project's selling points are: available now, hackable, repairable, no vendor lock-in, not price.

GLENEALY TOWER NO.1 GLENEALY CENTRAL HONG KONG'. Campaign AI disclosure: 'Some of the campaign images and promotional visuals for Atlas have been edited using AI-assisted tools'. findings.claim: Practical (non-legal) risk ranking for publishing: (1) HIGH and avoidable: using the word 'Atlas' in the project/model name, logo, repo name or cover image, or describing it as a 'replica/clone' of a named live commercial product in the same goods category; (2) MEDIUM: reusing any Atlas campaign photo/GIF/text, their lesson content, menu names ('Atlas Essentials') or a pixel-level copy of their UI; (3) LOW: building a functionally similar device from off-the-shelf parts with own case design and own UI. MakerWorld acts on third-party reports and can remove the model and revoke points. Comparable open projects use an own name + nominative reference + explicit non-affiliation line.
findings.evidence: MakerWorld Community Guidelines (primary): 'Copyright, trademark, or patent infringement', 'Impersonating individuals, brands, or official entities in a misleading way', and 'including using names, branding, or visual elements that may mislead others into believing you are affiliated with them'. Model Upload Guidelines: 'Using Non-Original Images: Using images created by others as model showcase images without authorization'. Exclusive agreement 5.5.4: 'An Exclusive Model may be removed due to violations of a third party's legitimate rights and interests and/or as a result of valid user or other third-party reports.' Precedents: CrossPoint Reader README: 'CrossPoint Reader is not affiliated with Xteink or any device manufacturer.'; FreeDeck: 'a Free/OpenSource replacement for Elgatos Streamdeck and similar'; OpenChess uses an own name and never names commercial boards. The recap currently frames the project as 'Replica open della scacchiera Atlas'. I did NOT search USPTO/EUIPO/HKIPD for an 'Atlas' registration.
findings.recommended_action: Pick an own project name now (repo is neutrally named 'eink-chess' already, good). In README/MakerWorld text use one sentence such as 'an open-source, build-it-yourself e-ink chess tablet, inspired by commercial e-ink chess devices such as Atlas; not affiliated with or endorsed by ZyvoraLabs, Lichess or Good Display'. Use only own photos/renders, own piece set with a GPL-compatible licence (e.g. the cburnett set, which Crosscheck ships as CC BY-SA 3.0), own menu wording, and a case that is visibly Fabrizio's design. Say 'works with Lichess' and do not use the Lichess logo as branding.

verification.corrected_claim: Same risk ranking (practical, non-legal): HIGH/avoidable = 'Atlas' in name/logo/cover or 'replica/clone of Atlas' framing (the recap currently says 'Replica open della scacchiera Atlas'); MEDIUM = reuse of campaign media, 'Atlas Essentials' wording or UI copy; LOW = functionally similar own design. MakerWorld removes on valid third-party reports (5.5.4) and bans 'Using Non-Original Images'. Correction: for the piece set use cburnett under its GPLv2+ grant (Lichess COPYING.md), not CC BY-SA 3.0, which is not GPL-compatible; Lichess logo may be used 'Only ... to refer to lichess.org'. Trademark registers were not searched.
verification.reasoning: Read MakerWorld Community Guidelines in the browser (WebFetch 403): 'Content that violates others' rights may be removed, including: Copyright, trademark, or patent infringement'; 'Impersonating individuals, brands, or official entities in a misleading way'; 'Impersonating MakerWorld or other official entities, including using names, branding, or visual elements that may mislead others into believing you are affiliated with them'. Model Upload Guidelines (wiki.bambulab.com, read in browser): 'Using Non-Original Images: Using images created by others as model showcase images without authorization, or failing to provide proof or explanation of authorization in the description.' Exclusive agreement 5.5.4 verbatim: 'An Exclusive Model may be removed due to violations of a third party's legitimate rights and interests and/or as a result of valid user or other third-party reports.' CrossPoint README: 'CrossPoint Reader is not affiliated with Xteink or any device manufacturer'. atlas-chess.com footer: 'ZYVORALABS LIMITED ... Hong Kong', '2026 (c) ZyvoraLabs'. Recap line 6 does say 'Replica open della scacchiera Atlas'. The ranking itself is the researcher's judgement (not a legal opinion) but is consistent with the primary texts. No trademark register search was done by me either. One correction in the recommended action: CC BY-SA 3.0 is NOT GPL-compatible (only BY-SA 4.0 -> GPLv3 one-way); however Lichess's COPYING.md lists 'public/piece/cburnett | Colin M.L. Burnett | GPLv2+', so take cburnett under GPLv2+ (compatible with a GPL-3.0 firmware), or a CC0/MIT set (rhosgfx CC0; fantasy/spatial/celtic MIT). COPYING.md also says the Lichess logo: 'Only use to refer to lichess.org'.

findings.claim: Licence chain is consistent with the plan: CT-800 is GPL-3.0-or-later (firmware, UCI version, tools AND opening book), GxEPD2 is GPL-3.0, so the combined firmware must be GPL-3.0(+). Two repo hygiene gaps before publishing: the repo has no LICENSE/COPYING file (README only says 'GPL-3.0'), and it contains a stray directory literally named '{src,docs}' from a failed brace expansion. Side note: Atlas itself ships CT-800, so its firmware is also bound by GPL-3.0 source-offer obligations.
findings.evidence: ct800.net/download.htm: 'The GNU General Public License (GPL) Version 3 or later applies to firmware, UCI version, all tools, and the opening book.'; current stable V1.46 (Aug 2024); ct800.net: 'The CT800, rated at about 2200 Elo'. findings.claim: MakerWorld Exclusive status is incompatible with an openly licensed / GitHub-hosted case: exclusive models must use the Standard Digital File License or the MakerWorld Exclusive License, may not be 'uploaded, shared, or made available on any other 3D model platform or channel', have a 90-day lock-in, and earn +25% points and boost value (cash-redeemable). The 14-Day Exclusive Launch variant gives +10% for a first-time release. Eligibility: account with >=100 cumulative prints, original work; exclusive guideline says AI-generated models and flat items are excluded and wants real print photos, a print profile and an assembly guide. Violations revoke all exclusive points for the model.
findings.evidence: Exclusive Model Program Agreement: 3.1 'total accumulated Model prints have reached at least 100'; 3.4.2 'which may be either: (a) the Standard Digital File License; or (b) the MakerWorld Exclusive License'; SDFL text: 'Users shall not share, sub-license, sell, rent, host, transfer, or distribute in any way the digital or 3D printed versions of this object, nor any other derivative work ... (including - but not limited to - remixes of this object, and hosting on other digital platforms)'; MakerWorld Exclusive License: derivatives allowed only if 'published, displayed, shared, and distributed exclusively on the MakerWorld Platform'; 5.3.1 'receive 25% more points'; 5.4 'period of no less than 90 days ("Lock-in Period")'; 6.3.1 '10% more points'; 5.5.1 'If an Exclusive Model is found to be directly or indirectly published on other platforms or websites ... considered "Non-Exclusive"' -> points revoked.
findings.recommended_action: Fabrizio must choose: (A) Exclusive on MakerWorld (SDFL or MW Exclusive License; STL/3MF/STEP live only on MakerWorld; GitHub repo contains firmware + docs + wiring only and links to the MakerWorld page for the shell) or (B) truly open hardware (CC BY-SA / CC BY-NC-SA on MakerWorld, STEP also on GitHub/Printables, no exclusive bonus). A is compatible with GPL firmware as long as no 3D files are in the repo. A middle path is the 14-day exclusive launch and then opening up, but check in the upload form whether the licence can be changed afterwards (SDFL grants are 'irrevocably granted').

verification.corrected_claim: As claimed, with two refinements: (1) the prohibition covers 'other platforms or websites' (5.5.1), so STL/3MF/STEP in the GitHub repo would break exclusivity; firmware/docs in the repo are not the Model; (2) the conflict is temporary, not permanent: after the 90-day lock-in (or the 14-day launch, which auto-expires) the creator may exit, keeps accrued exclusive points (5.4.2 / 6.4.2a), retains all rights (3.4.3) and can then publish under CC / on GitHub. Assembly guide is 'suggested', print profile and at least one real printed photo are required.
verification.reasoning: Read the full Exclusive Model Program Agreement in the browser. Verbatim: 3.1 'total accumulated Model prints have reached at least 100'; 2.2 'Exclusive Program Models may not be uploaded, shared, or made available on any other 3D model platform or channel for the duration of its participation in a Program'; 3.4.2 '(a) the Standard Digital File License; or (b) the MakerWorld Exclusive License'; SDFL text 'Users shall not share, sub-license, sell, rent, host, transfer, or distribute in any way ... (including - but not limited to - remixes of this object, and hosting on other digital platforms)' and 'irrevocably granted to the other users'; MW Exclusive License: derivatives only if 'published, displayed, shared, and distributed exclusively on the MakerWorld Platform'; 5.3.1/5.3.2 '25% more points' / '25% more value for each Boost', 5.3.3 cash-redeemable (7.2.1: 1 point = 0.066 USD, min 100 USD); 5.4 'no less than 90 days ("Lock-in Period")'; 5.5.1 'directly or indirectly published on other platforms or websites' (note: 'websites', so GitHub counts) -> all exclusive points for the model revoked; 6.3.1 '10% more points', 14-day Premier Lock-in; 8.2.1(c) AI-generated = non-original. Wiki guideline read: 'AI-generated content, Hueforges, plane/flat/2D models ... will be removed from the program'; 'All Exclusive Models require at least one photo of the actual printed model'; 'must include a Print Profile'; assembly guide is only 'suggested for all multi-part models'. Nuances: exclusivity is time-limited - 5.4.2 lets the creator exit after 90 days keeping accrued points ('All accrued Exclusive Points will remain unaffected'), and 3.4.3 says the creator 'retains all right, title, and interest', so the 'exclusive first, open later' path is contractually possible; the SDFL irrevocability concerns licences already granted to users, not the creator's right to relicense later (my reading, not legal advice). After the 14-day launch the model auto-exits (6.4.2a).

findings.claim: MakerWorld licences govern only the uploaded model files; GPL-3.0 firmware hosted on GitHub is a separate work and coexists with any MakerWorld licence. Linking a GitHub repo from the description is established practice: a live 7.5" ESP32 e-paper model (SDFL-licensed) links its repo and tells users where to get the precompiled firmware. There is no MakerWorld rule about firmware; the only relevant text is an account policy against excessive off-platform redirection, plus a ban on uploading non-model files as the model. Do not bundle GPL binaries/source inside an SDFL upload (SDFL forbids redistribution, GPL requires allowing it). The description editor accepts video URLs; raw file types accepted include 'zip' and 'py' but no firmware/bin type.
findings.evidence: Model 2443888 'Smart E-Paper Desk Dashboard (ESP32 - 7.5")': description says the Git repository is where you find everything and how to load the precompiled version; external link extracted from the page DOM: https://github.com/VoIPshare/ESP32-eInk-Dashboard; its licence block reads standard licence. Community Guidelines, Account Policies: 'Do not use your account to spam (e.g., excessive posting or low-quality content), promote excessively, or redirect users off-platform.' Upload guidelines: 'Incorrect Upload Scenario: Uploading non-model files for sharing, such as custom G-code, printer presets, or filament presets.' Upload wiki: 'Supported file types include 3ds, amf, dwg, dxf, f3d, ... py, ... step, stl, stp, studio3, zip, 3mf'; 'If you want to insert video media in the description, please paste the media URL'. CC licences exist on MakerWorld (guidelines mention 'No Derivatives', 'ShareAlike' and 'CC0' rules; CC0 requires 'photos of a personally printed physical object'); there is no GPL/software licence option mentioned in any MakerWorld document I read.
findings.recommended_action: MakerWorld page = shell + print profile + assembly guide + BOM + ONE prominent link to the GitHub repo/README, where the web-flasher link and wiring live. Keep firmware out of the MakerWorld upload. State both licences explicitly on both sides ('Case: <MakerWorld licence>. Firmware: GPL-3.0-or-later, source at <repo>').

findings.claim: MakerWorld's Bill of Materials block supports Maker's Supply items and free-form 'other parts'. Only Maker's Supply kits/parts earn anything: points = 200 x BOM price in USD once Downloads + 2xPrints reaches 2000, then 3-15% sales commission (Creator Program), a dedicated kit page at 3000. Our core parts (Good Display panel, FTS02, Seeed driver board, XIAO) are third-party and would be 'other parts' (no points). Maker's Supply and Exclusive incentives stack. No contest running on 21 Sep 2026 fits an electronics chess device.
findings.evidence: Upload wiki: 'check the option to add Bill of Materials, then choose kits and parts and filaments from Maker's Supply, or list other parts'. Incentive rules: 'Points Award = 200 x Total price of kits and parts in the BOM (calculated in USD)'; 'When the [Downloads + 2xPrints] reaches 2000'; commission 'varies from 3% to 15%'; 'you are allowed to participate in both Maker's Supply Incentive and Exclusive Model Incentive'; page banner notes a newer 'MakerWorld Creator Commission Incentives Rules' page supersedes it (not read). findings.claim: Web-flasher blocker in the current platformio.ini. pioarduino 55.03.38 automatically writes .pio/build/<env>/firmware.factory.bin after every build (no custom merge script needed), but it stamps the image with the board JSON's upload.flash_size. The project uses 'board = seeed_xiao_esp32s3' (flash_size 8MB) together with 'board_build.partitions = default_16MB.csv' (partitions end at 0x1000000). 'pio run -t upload' hides the mismatch because it passes '--flash-size detect', but ESP Web Tools flashes with flashSize 'keep', so a web-flashed unit keeps the 8 MB header and the bootloader rejects the partition table ('exceeds flash chip size') -> boot loop for every end user while it works on the developer's desk.
findings.evidence: ~/.platformio/platforms/espressif32/builder/main.py:1607-1663 'def esp32_create_combined_bin ... Uses esptool merge-bin to create a firmware.factory.bin that can be flashed at offset 0 ... flash_size = board.get("upload.flash_size", "4MB") ... "--flash-size", flash_size' and it is attached via 'env.AddPostAction(target_firm, silent_action)'; upload path lines ~1782: '"--flash-size", "detect"'. boards/seeed_xiao_esp32s3.json: '"flash_size": "8MB", "maximum_size": 8388608'; boards/seeed_xiao_esp32_s3_plus.json: '"flash_size": "16MB"', variant 'XIAO_ESP32S3_Plus', but '"partitions": "default_8MB.csv"'. default_16MB.csv: 'app1, app, ota_1, 0x650000,0x640000' / 'spiffs ... 0xc90000,0x360000' / 'coredump ... 0xFF0000,0x10000'. esp-web-tools src/flash.ts: 'await esploader.writeFlash({ fileArray, flashSize: "keep", flashMode: "keep", flashFreq: "keep", eraseAll: false, compress: true'. esp-idf v5.5 flash_partitions.c: 'if (pos->offset > chip_size || pos->offset + pos->size > chip_size) { ... "partition %d invalid - offset 0x%x size 0x%x exceeds flash chip size 0x%x" ... return ESP_ERR_INVALID_SIZE;' with 'chip_size = g_rom_flashchip.chip_size'. Not compiled or run (toolchain absent); conclusion is from reading the code paths.
findings.recommended_action: Change platformio.ini to 'board = seeed_xiao_esp32_s3_plus' and keep 'board_build.partitions = default_16MB.csv' (the Plus JSON defaults to the 8 MB table); this also selects the correct XIAO_ESP32S3_Plus variant with D11-D19. The memory_type/BOARD_HAS_PSRAM/USB flags in the ini then become redundant. Release artefact = firmware.factory.bin at offset 0. Add a release checklist step: erase a board and flash it ONLY through the web flasher before publishing.

verification.corrected_claim: As claimed: with board = seeed_xiao_esp32s3 the bootloader and firmware.factory.bin are stamped 8MB while default_16MB.csv places app1 up to 0xC90000; 'pio run -t upload' hides it via '--flash-size detect', but ESP Web Tools writes with flashSize 'keep', so the 2nd-stage bootloader (chip size taken from the image header) rejects partition 3 ('exceeds flash chip size 0x800000') and boot-loops. Fix: board = seeed_xiao_esp32_s3_plus + keep board_build.partitions = default_16MB.csv (or, minimally, board_upload.flash_size = 16MB). Also pin the platform to the pioarduino release URL (e.g. https://github.com/pioarduino/platform-espressif32/releases/download/55.03.38-1/platform-espressif32.zip) because unpinned 'platform = espressif32' builds something different on any other machine/CI. Verified by code reading only, not by flashing.
verification.reasoning: Re-read every code path. platformio.ini: 'board = seeed_xiao_esp32s3' + 'board_build.partitions = default_16MB.csv'. boards/seeed_xiao_esp32s3.json: upload.flash_size '8MB'; Plus JSON: '16MB', variant XIAO_ESP32S3_Plus, partitions default_8MB.csv. builder/main.py:1607-1663 esp32_create_combined_bin uses 'flash_size = board.get("upload.flash_size", "4MB")' -> 'merge-bin ... --flash-size flash_size' and is attached at :1693-1696 via env.AddPostAction(target_firm, ...); framework tools/pioarduino-build.py:108-109 also builds bootloader.bin with '--flash-size board_config.get("upload.flash_size")' (no prebuilt bootloader.bin exists in variants/XIAO_ESP32S3, only bootloader-tinyuf2.bin), so the header says 8MB. Upload path main.py:1782-1783 '--flash-size detect' masks it on the dev desk. No code in arduino.py/main.py adjusts flash_size from the partition CSV (grep). esp-web-tools src/flash.ts (main): 'flashSize: "keep", flashMode: "keep", flashFreq: "keep"'; esptool-js _updateImageFlashParams: if all three are keep -> 'Not changing the image'. ESP-IDF v5.5 bootloader_flash_config_esp32s3.c update_flash_config(): size from 'bootloader_hdr->spi_size' -> esp_rom_spiflash_config_param(... size*0x100000 ...); flash_partitions.c: 'chip_size = g_rom_flashchip.chip_size' and 'pos->offset + pos->size > chip_size' -> 'partition %d invalid ... exceeds flash chip size' -> ESP_ERR_INVALID_SIZE. With default_16MB.csv, app1 = 0x650000+0x640000 = 0xC90000 > 0x800000 -> partition 3 fails -> bootloader resets in a loop. Arduino core 3.3.8 is IDF 5.5-based (platform.json lists esp-idf v5.5.4). Not run on hardware (no toolchain), same caveat as the researcher. Additional issue found: platformio.ini has unpinned 'platform = espressif32'; on Fabrizio's Mac that resolves to the locally installed pioarduino 55.03.38 (.piopm uri github.com/pioarduino/.../55.03.38-1), but on CI or another user's machine it resolves to the official PlatformIO registry platform (older Arduino core, different builder, no guarantee of firmware.factory.bin or of the Plus board JSON). Minor: the BOARD_HAS_PSRAM/CDC_ON_BOOT/memory_type lines are already redundant with the non-Plus JSON too.

findings.claim: ESP Web Tools is a fit for the MakerWorld audience: manifest supports chipFamily 'ESP32-S3' and an optional serialType 'cdc'|'uart'; esptool-js auto-enters the bootloader over the S3's built-in USB-Serial/JTAG (VID 0x303A, PID 0x1001), which is what the XIAO board definition selects (ARDUINO_USB_MODE=1). Requirements: HTTPS page, desktop Chromium-class browser with Web Serial (not iOS), binaries served same-origin or with CORS (so commit them to the GitHub Pages site, do not point at GitHub Release asset URLs). Improv-Serial lets the same page push Wi-Fi credentials right after flashing. Risks to test on real hardware: an open 2023 issue reports 'device has been lost' at the end of S3 native-USB flashing; and once we add deep sleep the USB port disappears while asleep, so users need BOOT/RESET access.
findings.evidence: esp-web-tools src/const.ts: 'chipFamily: "ESP32" | ... | "ESP32-C5" | ... | "ESP32-S3" | "ESP8266"; parts: { path: string; offset: number; }[]; serialType?: "cdc" | "uart";' and Manifest fields 'new_install_prompt_erase', 'new_install_improv_wait_time', 'funding_url'. Docs: 'ESP Web Tools requires that your website is served over https://'; 'If your manifest or the firmware files are hosted on another server, make sure you configure the CORS-headers'; 'Web Serial is available in Mozilla Firefox, Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge browsers (but not on your iOS device)'; 'If the firmware supports Improv, a user will be asked to connect the device to the network after installing the firmware'; script 'https://unpkg.com/esp-web-tools@10/dist/web/install-button.js?module'. esptool-js esploader.ts: 'export const USB_JTAG_SERIAL_PID = 0x1001;' and 'if (mode === "usb_reset" || this.isUsbJtagSerialPort()) { ... usbJTAGSerialReset'. Board JSON: '-DARDUINO_USB_MODE=1', '-DARDUINO_USB_CDC_ON_BOOT=1'. Issue esphome/esp-web-tools#331 (open since 2023-02): 'Installation failed, The device has been lost' on S3 native USB. esptool docs: 'The USB-Serial/JTAG peripheral can only trigger a core reset, which does not re-sample the state of the boot strapping pin' (manual BOOT entry needs a manual reset afterwards). Seeed wiki: 'Press and hold the BOOT button ... then connect to the computer'. Precedents: OpenChess 'https://joojoooo.github.io/OpenChess/flash.html' (GitHub Pages, 'A Chromium browser (Chrome, Edge, Opera)'), CrossPoint 'https://crosspointreader.com/#flash-tools'.
findings.recommended_action: Add a /docs (GitHub Pages) flasher: index.html with <esp-web-install-button manifest="manifest.json">, manifest {name, version, new_install_prompt_erase:true, builds:[{chipFamily:"ESP32-S3", parts:[{path:"firmware.factory.bin", offset:0}]}]}; if assets move to LittleFS add a second part at offset 13172736 (0xC90000 in default_16MB.csv; JSON needs decimal). Build and publish via GitHub Actions on tag. Keep USB in hardware-CDC mode (never TinyUSB) so auto-reset works. Implement Improv-Serial in firmware as the primary Wi-Fi setup with captive portal as fallback, and consider letting the flasher page also send the Lichess token over Web Serial so nobody types a token on e-ink. CASE REQUIREMENT for Fabrizio: two pin-holes over the XIAO BOOT and RESET buttons plus the USB-C cut-out, otherwise a bad flash or deep-sleeping unit means opening the shell. Keep 'pio run -t upload' and the Espressif esptool-js demo page as documented fallbacks.

verification.corrected_claim: As claimed, with small corrections: the ESP Web Tools docs now list Firefox alongside Chrome and Edge for Web Serial (still not iOS), so 'Chromium only' is outdated per the docs (test Firefox before promising it); issue #331 (open since 2023-02-10) reports 'The device has been lost' mid-transfer on S3 native USB on Windows while plain esptool-js worked on the same boards, so it is a risk to test, not a known blocker. A manually entered download mode over USB-Serial/JTAG needs a manual RESET afterwards (core reset does not re-sample the strapping pin), hence BOOT+RESET access holes in the case. Manifest: chipFamily 'ESP32-S3', parts [{path: firmware.factory.bin, offset: 0}], optional LittleFS part at 13172736 (0xC90000).
verification.reasoning: Re-fetched sources. esp-web-tools src/const.ts: Build has chipFamily union incl. 'ESP32-S3', parts {path, offset}, and 'serialType?: "cdc" | "uart"'; Manifest has funding_url, new_install_skip_erase, new_install_prompt_erase, new_install_improv_wait_time. Docs site: 'ESP Web Tools requires that your website is served over https://'; CORS header instruction; 'Web Serial is available in Mozilla Firefox, Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge browsers (but not on your iOS device)'; Improv: 'a user will be asked to connect the device to the network'; script unpkg esp-web-tools@10. esptool-js esploader.ts: 'export const USB_JTAG_SERIAL_PID = 0x1001', ESPRESSIF_VID 0x303a, 'if (mode === "usb_reset" || this.isUsbJtagSerialPort())' -> usbJTAGSerialReset. Board JSON (local): -DARDUINO_USB_MODE=1, -DARDUINO_USB_CDC_ON_BOOT=1 (HW CDC = the fixed-function USB-Serial/JTAG peripheral, which enumerates as 303A:1001 - inference; the JSON hwids 0x2886:0x0056 are the TinyUSB IDs). Issue #331: title 'Firmware programming using native USB port on ESP32-S3 does not work', open since 2023-02-10, error 'Installation failed, The device has been lost' - but the reporter describes failure MID-transfer (speed surge then disconnect), not 'at the end', and says esptool-js itself works on the same hardware. esptool troubleshooting doc: 'The USB-Serial/JTAG peripheral can only trigger a core reset, which does not re-sample the state of the boot strapping pin' (fix: --after watchdog-reset or press EN/power-cycle). 0xC90000 = 13172736 checked. OpenChess flasher URL https://joojoooo.github.io/OpenChess/flash.html and CrossPoint https://crosspointreader.com/#flash-tools confirmed. Seeed driver-board wiki shows no BOOT/RESET breakout, so case access holes to the XIAO buttons are indeed needed. Depends on T4-FACTORY-BIN-FLASHSIZE being fixed first (web flasher uses flashSize 'keep'). GitHub release assets lacking CORS headers is common knowledge, not re-verified by me.

findings.claim: The most relevant prior art is ChuckJonas/crosscheck (MIT): a working Lichess Board-API client on near-identical hardware (ESP32-S3, 8 MB PSRAM, 480x800 e-ink, GT911 touch, UC8179 mentioned in its notes). Measured/verified lessons: (a) full-frame fast refresh 562 ms; a render must block until the panel finishes or the next frame ghosts ('the OLD plane got the new frame and changed pixels were not driven'); (b) they REMOVED periodic full refresh because 'the every-eighth-update flash ... read as random flashes' and now full-refresh only at game start/end, board flip and a manual menu item, whereas our phase 1 full-refreshes every 20 moves; (c) highlights drawn as borders, not fills, to survive ghosting; 4 px dead zone at square edges and immediate selected-piece feedback for 60 px squares; touch polled, never blocked by render; (d) Lichess: open seeks under ~8 minutes estimated are rejected with 400 'Invalid time control' (verified 2026-09-11 for 3+0, 3+2, 5+0), matching the official rule that Board API seeks are Rapid/Classical/Correspondence only, blitz only for direct challenges and AI; (e) event stream + game stream + a command connection; Lichess drops idle connections after ~10 s so they send a keep-alive every 5 s, otherwise each move costs a ~1 s TLS handshake instead of 0.2 s; (f) Wi-Fi modem sleep stalls the stream, so disable it during games only; (g) heap: 231 KB free before Wi-Fi, 160 KB with Wi-Fi, 144 KB with both streams open; (h) clocks redrawn every 1-10 s (default 5), every second under 20 s; (i) token scopes used: board:play, challenge:write, challenge:read, puzzle:read, puzzle:write, study:read, follow:read; token typed on an on-screen keyboard or dropped as JSON on SD. Other projects: rtens/crosspoint-reader-chess (MIT, ESP32-C3, side buttons, 'movesUntilRefresh' default 20, Lichess puzzles fetched in batches of 50, engine plays random moves only); joojoooo/OpenChess (physical board, Lichess + web flasher on GitHub Pages, code MIT + PolyForm-Noncommercial); larsi-org/cyd-chess (micro-Max 4.8, rules/engine/book/undo kept display-independent and tested off-device with g++); MakerWorld model 2443888 author reports colour e-paper partial refresh is useless (5-6 s) and moved to B/W.
findings.evidence: Quotes above are from crosscheck docs/crosscheck-dev-notes.md and docs/crosscheck-spec.md ('ESP32-S3, 8 MB PSRAM, 480x800 16-gray e-ink, GT911 touch'; 'Lichess stream stalls under modem sleep ... High likelihood'; 'design highlights as borders rather than fills'; 'Add a 4 px dead zone at square edges'). Lichess API spec, Board tag: 'Rapid, Classical and Correspondence' ... 'For direct challenges, games vs AI, and bulk pairing, Blitz is also possible'. Our README: 'Ogni 20 mosse un full refresh per pulire il ghosting.' crosspoint-reader-chess README: 'currently only with random moves by engine'. cyd-chess README: 'chess_rules/micromax/book/undo/persistence have no display or touch dependency at all, so they're usable and testable independent of the ESP32 side.' I found no Hackaday article on a DIY e-ink touch chess device.
findings.recommended_action: Read crosscheck's two docs before writing phase 3; its MIT code can be studied and even reused inside a GPL-3.0 project (keep the MIT notice). Concretely: replace the fixed every-20-moves full refresh with full refresh at natural boundaries + a manual 'clean screen' action; border-style highlights; square dead zone; keep-alive on the command connection; modem sleep off only in-game; UI must offer only >=10+0-class seeks and route faster play through 'challenge AI / challenge friend'. Structure rules + CT-800 glue as a hardware-free library with a PlatformIO [env:native] test target, which is doubly useful here because the xtensa toolchain is not installed on this Mac.

verification.corrected_claim: As claimed, with two refinements: (1) crosscheck targets the Xteink X4 Pro e-reader (ESP32-S3, 8 MB PSRAM, 480x800 16-gray e-ink, GT911, UC8179, SD card, own display driver, fork of CrossPoint) - same MCU/touch/controller family but not our panel or GxEPD2, so its 562 ms full-frame figure and heap numbers are indicative only; (2) the Board API seek floor is 'estimated game duration >= 8 minutes' (time + 40 x increment >= 480 s, i.e. Rapid), so the seek menu may offer 8+0, 7+2, 5+5, 10+0 and slower; anything faster must go through direct challenge or challenge-AI. All quoted lessons (blocking render vs OLD-plane ghosting, no periodic full refresh, border highlights, 4 px dead zone, 5 s keep-alive vs ~10 s idle drop, modem sleep off in-game, 231/160/144 KB heap, clock cadence, token scopes) were re-read verbatim in the crosscheck docs.
verification.reasoning: Re-fetched crosscheck README, dev notes and spec. README: 'A Lichess client for the Xteink X4 Pro e-reader', MIT, fork of CrossPoint Reader, cburnett pieces stated as CC BY-SA 3.0. Spec: 'Xteink X4 Pro (ESP32-S3, 8 MB PSRAM, 480x800 16-gray e-ink, GT911 touch)', 60 px squares, 'a 4 px dead zone at square edges', highlights as 'borders rather than fills', expected partial '200-300 ms', '~0.5 s per move', modem sleep on in lobby/off in game. Dev notes verbatim: 'A fast refresh takes 562 ms on the panel' (full frame because 'the UC8179 driver of the X4 Pro does not implement [windowed refresh]'); 'the OLD plane got the new frame and changed pixels were not driven'; 'There is no periodic full refresh: the every-eighth-update flash of earlier builds read as random flashes during play'; 'Lichess refuses open seeks under 8 minutes estimated with a 400 "Invalid time control" (verified on 2026-09-11 for 3+0, 3+2, and 5+0)'; keep-alive 'every 5 seconds', Lichess 'drops an idle connection after about ten seconds', 'about 1 s instead of 0.2 s'; heap '231 KB free before Wi-Fi, 160 KB with Wi-Fi and the client tasks, 144 KB with both streams open'; clocks 'every clockRefreshSec seconds (1, 2, 5, or 10; default 5)' and every second under 20 s; scopes 'board:play, challenge:write, challenge:read, puzzle:read, puzzle:write, study:read, follow:read'; token via on-screen keyboard or SD JSON. Lichess yaml: 'Rapid, Classical and Correspondence only...'. Our README line 30: 'Ogni 20 mosse un full refresh' and main.cpp:80 '% 20'. rtens/crosspoint-reader-chess: MIT, ESP32-C3 Xteink X4/X3, movesUntilRefresh 20, batches of 50, 'currently only with random moves by engine'. cyd-chess: micro-Max 4.8, the no-display-dependency sentence, g++ harnesses. MakerWorld 2443888 author comment (read in browser, auto-translated): partial refresh on colour panel 'still have to wait 5-6 seconds, so it is almost useless ... switched to a black and white display'. OpenChess: original MIT + joojoooo modifications PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0, Lichess, GitHub Pages flasher. Caveats: 'near-identical hardware' is overstated - it is a commercial e-reader with a 16-gray panel, its own display driver (not GxEPD2) and an SD card; heap/refresh numbers do not transfer 1:1. The recommendation 'offer only >=10+0-class seeks' is too strict: the observed limit is estimated duration (time + 40 x increment) >= 480 s = Lichess Rapid, so 8+0, 7+2 and 5+5 qualify (inference from the Lichess speed definition plus the crosscheck note 'under 8 minutes estimated').

unknowns: Atlas real battery capacity (creator says 4000 mAh in the spec image and 2000 mAh in FAQ + website), exact e-paper/touch part numbers, whether it has frontlight or sound, which time controls it offers, how Lichess login is done on-device (OAuth vs token), and whether ZyvoraLabs will publish GPL source for their CT-800-based firmware.

Whether 'Atlas' (or the stylised ATLAS logo) is a registered or pending trademark for chess devices/electronics in the EU, US or Hong Kong, and whether the enclosure has a registered design: no trademark/design database was searched.

Also whether the post-flash hard reset reliably restarts the app over USB-Serial/JTAG without pressing RESET.

questions_for_user: Project name: are you OK dropping 'Atlas'/'replica' from every public surface and shipping under an own name (CollectiCraft-branded or neutral)? Do you have a name in mind?

MakerWorld strategy: Exclusive (Standard Digital File or MakerWorld Exclusive License, +25% points, 90-day lock-in, shell files may NOT be on GitHub/Printables) or truly open hardware (CC licence, STEP also on GitHub, no exclusive bonus)? Does your account already have >=100 cumulative prints?

Do you intend to sell anything around this (printed shells, kits, assembled units), or is it purely a free model? That changes the licence choice (NC or not) and how careful we must be about the Atlas association.
Orientation: portrait handheld like Atlas (board on top, controls below) or landscape desk device with a side column (what phase 1 does now)? Or both via two shell variants?

Wake/power UX: is the driver board's slide switch enough for you, or do you want an Atlas-style wake button (one extra tactile switch + 2 wires), or wake-by-touch (requires moving the touch INT wire to a different pin now, before wiring)?

Build skill target for MakerWorld users: must the build be solder-free? In particular, did you order the XIAO ESP32-S3 Plus with pre-soldered headers, and are you OK asking users to solder the XIAO headers and the buzzer?

Rank the Atlas features we are missing by how much YOU care: local two-player, challenge a friend / receive invites, play Lichess AI, offline puzzle pack, openings/endgames/classics lessons, take-over-position vs engine, analysis/review, PGN upload from phone.

Where should the web flasher live: a GitHub Pages site under your own GitHub account/organisation (which one?) or a CollectiCraft domain? And should the UI/README be English-only or English + Italian?

Do you have a Lichess account (and a second account or a friend) available for testing seeks/challenges, and are you fine with the Board API limit that random-opponent games must be rapid or slower (roughly 10+0 and up)?
